name: theology
tier_note: Tiers = STORY difficulty (T1 = a named figure + one dramatic beat a kid can picture .. T5 = the deep story with civilizational or mythic weight and pointed named specifics), NOT obscurity. Grade-10 HARD ceiling: no academic theology jargon (supralapsarianism, perichoresis, filioque, hypostatic union, kenosis, theosis-as-term) -- doctrine appears only as STORY (Athanasius vs Arius at Nicaea 325 OK, abstract 'homoousios' NOT). Aim ~30%+ of rungs at T1-T2 (every named figure gets a T1/T2 foundational anchor before being referenced at T3+; per §16 teach-before-test). Operative gameplay gate = TOTAL record chars (stem + 4 choices): T1<=460, T2<=680, T3<=850, T4<=1000, T5<=1150; context is UNCAPPED (read only AFTER the answer, off the timer). Theology is THRESHOLD mode (praying at altars), ~65s timer at WIS 10 (SUBJECT_TIMER 48 + 1.7/WIS -- most generous in the game by design; theology + mythology stems carry dense scaffolded narrative); no same-FACT repeats within a ladder (same-TOPIC deepening is the goal; each rung a DIFFERENT beat of the story).
voice_rule:
THEOLOGY = the WONDER PATTERN, STORY-LED: the most memorable theology question reveals the most specific cool fact about a story kids should know. This bank is a kid's gateway to WESTERN mythological + legendary heritage -- not a doctrine quiz, not an author-attribution quiz, not comparative religion. STORY-LED.
  ANSWER HIERARCHY (Wonder Pattern):
  (1) NAMED THINGS (highest) -- specific quotes ('This is my body', 'Eighty and six years I have served Him', 'Kiss me, Hardy' from Nelson is out-of-lane but the shape is right, e.g. Polycarp's 'Eighty and six years I have served Him'), named objects (Excalibur, Mjolnir, Holy Grail, Olifant, Pandora's jar, Durendal, the Lance of Longinus, Gae Bolg, the Salmon of Knowledge), named epithets (Odin 'All-Father', Thor 'Hammer-Wielder', Achilles 'Swift-Footed', Lancelot 'of the Lake', Cuchulainn 'Hound of Ulster').
  (2) VIVID ACTIONS -- Hercules strangling the Nemean Lion bare-handed; Thor in a wedding-veil disguise to recover Mjolnir; Robin splitting his own arrow at the Sheriff's tournament; Daniel sealed overnight with lions; Polycarp at 86 walking to the stake; Odin spitting the Mead of Poetry from his beak; Cuchulainn's ristrad (warp-spasm); the Salmon of Knowledge cooking on Fionn's spit; Diarmuid killed by the boar of Ben Bulben.
  (3) OBJECTS / MATERIALS -- Mjolnir's making by Sindri + Brokkr; the Round Table's Siege Perilous reserved for Galahad; Apollo's lyre from Hermes's tortoise-shell; the Shroud of Turin; Sherwood's longbow; the Ard Ri's coronation stone at Tara.
  (4) NUMBERS (singular + unforgettable) -- 12 labors of Hercules; 12 apostles; 9 worlds of Yggdrasil; 24 hours Daniel in the den; 40 days in the wilderness; 30 pieces of silver; the Fianna's four qualifications.
  (5) GENERIC LABELS -- BANNED as primary answers ('Trinitarianism', 'transubstantiation', 'the doctrine of X', 'a Christian belief', 'a Norse myth').
  THE DINNER TEST: does the ANSWER ALONE make a parent ask 'wait, what?' If 'the Trinity' stops conversation cold but 'Polycarp saying eighty and six years I have served Him' makes them ask WHO, you wrote the wrong question.
  STORY-NOT-ATTRIBUTION TEST: am I asking about the STORY (what happened) or about authorship/citation (who wrote/said it)? If the latter, REWRITE TO STORY. No 'Who wrote the Iliad?', 'Who said Here I stand?'.
  TWO ladder SHAPES:
  (A) FIGURE/STORY/ARTIFACT ladder -- ONE figure, story, or object deepened across tiers: Polycarp's martyrdom (T1 who was he -> T2 what did he say -> T3 the pyre and the sword -> T4 the Smyrna crowd's part -> T5 what the letter from Smyrna says he did); Excalibur (T1 sword in the stone -> T2 the Lady of the Lake -> T3 the scabbard's magic -> T4 Bedivere returning the blade -> T5 what breaks and what returns).
  (B) CONCEPT/THEME ladder -- ONE mythic pattern deepened ACROSS cases: dying-and-rising figures (Balder / Persephone / Christ); heroic-descent-into-the-underworld (Orpheus / Aeneas / Christ's Harrowing / Odin at Mimir's well); sworn-brotherhoods (Achilles + Patroclus / David + Jonathan / Roland + Oliver / Fionn's Fianna); geis + oath-breaking as doom (Cuchulainn's geasa / Roland refusing the Olifant / Peter's denial). Theme ladders carry the analytic backbone (~25%+) and native T4/T5 ceiling.
  SCENE-LED, NEVER DEFINITION-SHELL: HARD BANS on cold stems -- 'What is the doctrine of X?' / 'Who wrote the Y?' / 'In what year...?' / bare definition-recall of any kind. ALWAYS a scene then a pointed question. INVERT THE WONDER: put the astonishing named detail in the STEM as the hook and ask the knowable thing.
  ONE COHERENT WONDER PER RUNG: hook + setup + answer are the SAME beat; two facts = two rungs; no decoration-mismatch (an interesting-but-unrelated detail stapled in front of a different answer is BANNED); no theology-stacking.
  WONDER-IN-STEM-NOT-CONTEXT: the substantive story beat lives in the STEM; context (after the answer, off the timer) may deepen it but never carry it.
  DISTRACTOR & ANTI-RESTATEMENT DISCIPLINE (KNOWLEDGE subject -- deducing the answer from the stem IS the tell): the stem sets up the SCENE, never the ANSWER the choice names; if the stem describes the deed and the answer merely names it, that is RESTATEMENT. ALL FOUR choices stay LIVE given everything the stem says; never DEFINE a figure then ask his name. DISTRACTORS ARE ADJACENT-BUT-WRONG REAL FIGURES / OBJECTS / QUOTES: other saints, other heroes, other gods, other artifacts, other tales -- used HONESTLY (a real Grail knight vs a wrong Grail knight, real quotes from real martyrs, real named swords from real epics). Never joke options. CHOICE PARITY: all four structurally parallel (answer a named figure -> all four named figures; no lone-long, lone-number standout).
  §14 STORY-IN-STEM, §15 NO WEASEL CLOSERS ('What did he say?' not 'What's the takeaway?'), §16 TEACH-BEFORE-TEST (every major named figure -- Polycarp, Hercules, Thor, Roland, Robin Hood, Galahad, Cuchulainn, Fionn, Lugh, the Dagda -- needs a T1 or T2 foundational anchor before being referenced at T3+).
  ACCURACY RAILS (non-negotiable -- this is for real children): every name, story, quote, and artifact REAL and correctly attributed to the source tradition; NO fabricated legends or unsourced quotes; famous MYTHS are told AS the myths they are (Excalibur = ONE version, Grail = varying versions across Chretien/Malory/Wolfram named honestly; the Balder mistletoe story from Snorri's Prose Edda, not invented); no confusing figures across traditions; no fusing Celtic Tuatha figures with Norse figures.
  LANE BORDERS (five shipped sisters share this world -- respect the borders): HISTORY covers actual wars, empires, treaties, kings-as-heads-of-state; theology covers the STORIES that survived from those eras (Roland at Roncesvalles as CHANSON, not military history; the Crusade of the Cross as story of Bernard of Clairvaux and the child crusades, not campaign geography). GEOGRAPHY covers sacred sites AS PLACES (Mecca, Jerusalem, Kailash, Angkor Wat, Notre Dame, Tara Hill, Skellig Michael) -- theology covers what HAPPENED at them in story (the Ark landing on Ararat = theology; Ararat as a place = geography). PHILOSOPHY covers moral reasoning; theology covers moral reasoning INSIDE a story (Job's argument WITH God = theology; the problem of evil as reasoning move = philosophy). Kings-and-battles-as-history overlaps: flag any Charlemagne / Alfred / Arthur / Aethelstan / Beowulf overlap in history_overlap and key DIFFERENT facts (theology owns the STORY beats -- Roland at the pass, Alfred and the cakes as legend, Aethelstan's coronation-cup blessing).
  OUT entirely: comparative religion (Islam, Buddhism, Hinduism, non-Western traditions = out of scope, different bank if ever built); modern cults (Jonestown, Heaven's Gate, Aum -- history not theology-heritage); doctrine quizzing without a story anchor; author-attribution recall; academic theology jargon; smug atheist voice; smug believer voice; Christian-doctrinal framings ('fulfilled the prophecy', 'the Lord', 'Our Lord', 'the Savior', 'the true God', 'the risen Christ' -- use plain narrative Jesus / Paul / the bishop Polycarp); metaphysics adjudication between traditions.
framing:
The theology bank is a kid's gateway to the WESTERN MYTHOLOGICAL + LEGENDARY HERITAGE. Brandon is NOT Christian; the bank explicitly does NOT promote Christianity as metaphysically true. ALL FOUR pillars are presented on the SAME PLANE with the same narrative voice -- Christian, Greek, Norse, and Western-mythological (Arthurian + Robin Hood + Celtic/Irish) -- with full dramatic seriousness, named details intact, no 'this one is real, these are myth' framing. Cultural heritage is the frame: these are the bodies of narrative that shaped Western imagination and kids should know them because of that cultural weight, NOT because the bank endorses any one tradition's truth-claims.
  SYMMETRIC-VOICE TEST (apply to every Christian-tradition question): would you write the equivalent Greek or Norse or Celtic story the same way? If 'fulfilled the prophecy of Zechariah' feels weird restated as 'fulfilled the prophecy of the Pythia at Delphi' or 'fulfilled the geis Deirdre foretold', DROP 'fulfilled' -- use 'echoes' or 'matches the figure in' instead. If 'the Lord told Moses' feels weird as 'the Lord told Odysseus' or 'the Lord told Cuchulainn', use 'Jesus' / 'Paul' / 'the bishop' -- parallel narrative voice across all four pillars.
  PILLAR SHARES (~300-350 topics total, ~2,500-3,000 Q, matching the wonder-bank scale of geography/science/animal/cooking):
  P1 CHRISTIAN STORIES ~40% (~120-140 topics) -- Old Testament narratives (Noah, Abraham, Joseph, Moses, Joshua, David, Elijah, Daniel, Jonah, Esther); New Testament (Jesus stories, parables, the Passion, Paul's journeys and shipwreck, Stephen's stoning, Peter's denial and restoration); saint legends (Polycarp of Smyrna, Sebastian, Lawrence and the gridiron, Joan of Arc, Patrick and the snakes-legend, George and the dragon, Francis of Assisi and the wolf of Gubbio, Becket at Canterbury, Christopher and the child, Nicholas of Myra, Perpetua and Felicity, Anthony of the desert); Christian symbolism when it lives in a STORY (the fish sign in the persecutions, the labarum on Constantine's shields, the wafer + wine at the Last Supper as scene). LARGEST SHARE because of cultural weight and because it's the tradition Brandon's kids will most often encounter -- NOT because it's endorsed as true.
  P2 GREEK MYTHOLOGY ~20% (~60-70 topics) -- Olympians (Zeus, Hera, Poseidon, Athena, Apollo, Artemis, Hermes, Aphrodite, Ares, Hephaestus, Dionysus, Demeter, Hades); Titans (Cronus, Prometheus, Atlas); Trojan War cycle (Achilles + Patroclus + Hector, the Judgment of Paris, the wooden horse, the sack); Odyssey (Cyclops, Sirens, Circe, Scylla + Charybdis, Ithaca return, Argus the dog); Hercules's 12 labors named individually; Perseus + Medusa + Andromeda; Theseus + Minotaur + Ariadne's thread; Persephone + pomegranate; Orpheus + Eurydice; Prometheus's liver; Pandora's jar; Atalanta and the golden apples; Jason + Argonauts + the Golden Fleece; Bellerophon + Pegasus.
  P3 NORSE MYTHOLOGY ~20% (~60-70 topics) -- Aesir (Odin, Frigg, Thor, Baldr, Tyr, Heimdall, Bragi, Idunn, Forseti); Vanir (Freyr, Freyja, Njord); Loki tricks (Sif's hair, Sleipnir's siring, the wall-builder, Baldr's death); the great artifacts (Mjolnir by Sindri + Brokkr, Gungnir, Draupnir, Skidbladnir, Bifrost, Gjallarhorn); the nine worlds of Yggdrasil (Asgard, Midgard, Jotunheim, Alfheim, Svartalfheim, Vanaheim, Muspelheim, Niflheim, Helheim); Ragnarok (Fenrir on Odin, Thor on Jormungandr, Surt's fire); Sigurd + Fafnir + the ring cycle (proto-Volsung); the Mead of Poetry (Odin the eagle spitting it into the vats); Beowulf (Grendel, Grendel's mother, the dragon).
  P4 WESTERN MYTHOLOGY ~20% (~60-70 topics) -- ARTHURIAN: Excalibur (sword in the stone AND the Lady of the Lake, both versions honest), Round Table + Siege Perilous, the Grail quest across Chretien / Malory / Wolfram (Perceval / Bors / Galahad), Lancelot + Guinevere, Merlin + Nimue, Mordred + Camlann, Bedivere returning the sword. ROBIN HOOD: Sherwood + the Merry Men (Little John, Friar Tuck, Will Scarlet, Alan-a-Dale, Maid Marian), the Sheriff of Nottingham, the arrow-splitting tournament, Fitzwarin as historical anchor. WESTERN-MEDIEVAL LEGEND: Roland at Roncesvalles (Olifant + Durendal), El Cid + Tizona, Faust + Mephistopheles, William Tell + the apple. CELTIC / IRISH MYTHOLOGY -- Tuatha De Danann (Lugh Lamhfhada + the spear that never missed, Dagda + the cauldron of plenty, Nuada Silver-Arm, Danu, the Morrigan, Manannan mac Lir, Aengus Og + the swans, Brigid + the flame at Kildare), Cuchulainn (the Tain Bo Cuailnge cattle-raid, Gae Bolg the belly-spear, ristrad the warp-spasm, the geasa he broke, death tied standing to a stone with the raven), the Fianna (Fionn mac Cumhaill + the Salmon of Knowledge burning his thumb, Diarmuid + Grainne + the boar of Ben Bulben, Oisin + Niamh + Tir na nOg + the three centuries in a day). Coverage across the pillar is BALANCED -- Arthurian ~25% of P4, Robin Hood + Roland/El Cid/Faust/Tell ~25%, Celtic-Irish ~50% (deliberately generous because these are the most underrepresented in modern kid education despite being the DEEPEST vein of Western myth).
  STANCE (SUPREME per moral_vision.md sec 6 + 9):
  NO SMUG ATHEIST VOICE -- no 'primitive belief', no 'people used to think', no scare-quoted 'God', no 'superstition'. Religious and mythological thought is taken seriously on its own terms as story.
  NO SMUG BELIEVER VOICE -- no 'and that's why X tradition has the answer', no prophecy-fulfillment doctrinal language in the bank's own voice. Stories are PRESENTED, not advertised.
  BANNED CHRISTIAN-DOCTRINAL FRAMINGS: 'fulfilled the prophecy', 'the Lord', 'Our Lord', 'the Savior', 'the true God', 'the risen Christ', 'the Word became flesh'. Use PLAIN NARRATIVE: 'Jesus', 'Paul', 'the bishop Polycarp', 'the crowd at Smyrna'.
  BANNED SMUG-ATHEIST FRAMINGS: 'primitive belief', 'people used to think', scare quotes around any religious term, 'the myth of' (except when literally naming a myth like 'the myth of Persephone'), 'debunked'.
  ALL FOUR PILLARS EQUAL DRAMATIC SERIOUSNESS: Balder's mistletoe death carries the same weight as Christ's crucifixion in this bank's voice; Cuchulainn dying standing tied to a stone carries the same weight as Polycarp walking to the stake; Ragnarok as an ending carries the same weight as the Book of Revelation.
  HONEST HARD DETAILS (the dark and bright equally): Salem 1692, Cathar Albigensian crusade, Aztec-style human sacrifice IS out of scope (non-Western pillar), Norse thrall-sacrifice at funerals CAN appear as story-detail without lingering, Cuchulainn's ristrad body-horror CAN appear (kids can handle it -- Norse and Celtic myth are LOUD), the Christian martyrdoms in full sensory detail (Sebastian's arrows, Lawrence's gridiron 'turn me over, I am done on this side', Perpetua steadying the sword hand of her nervous executioner). Grade-10 kids can HANDLE these; the bank does not soften.
  OUT: any hint that one tradition is truer than another; any doctrine-quizzing without a story anchor; author-attribution ('Who wrote Beowulf?', 'Who wrote the Iliad?' -- ask about STORIES); modern cult content (Jonestown / Heaven's Gate / Aum -- history bank); academic theology jargon (supralapsarianism / hypostatic union / filioque / kenosis / theosis-as-term / homoousios-as-term -- doctrine only as STORY, Athanasius at Nicaea OK); comparative-religion adjudication.
  MARK STANCE TOPICS `vision_mandated: true` so the moral audit checks them BOTH DIRECTIONS -- imposed Christian-verdict AND smug-atheist-verdict.
